title: NBA Washed Meter: Which late-30s (and older) stars still got it? And who's on the decline? - CBS Sports
description: LeBron James, Stephen Curry, James Harden and more big names are playing big roles ... and some look better than
body:
LeBron James, Stephen Curry, James Harden and more big names are playing big roles ... and some look better than others
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:30 am ET
                        
                •
            
            11 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        We're in an age of outliers when it comes to aging superstars. Injuries are as persistent a problem in the NBA as they've ever been, yet the league is somehow also loaded with big names retaining relevance deep into their 30s (and in one notable case, beyond). Remember when the 2024 Olympics was supposed to be the swan song for LeBron James, Stephen Curry and Kevin Durant as the faces of the NBA? They're currently leading teams with a combined record of 27-10.Some of the old guys very clearly still have it. Others are starting to slip. There are nine former All-NBA players in their age-36 season or later, so let's check in with each of them and measure how much they've had left in the tank thus far this season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Stephen Curry (Age: 38)Washed meter: 0 out of 10
We're choosing to ignore injuries here, though they've obviously become a persistent issue for Curry. When he's been on the court, Curry has been closer to his peak than anyone on this list. Even after leaving Wednesday's loss to the Houston Rockets after five minutes, he's still averaging more than a point per minute. He has a higher effective field goal percentage than he did when he became the NBA's first unanimous MVP in 2016. He's even trimmed his turnover rate to a career-low. He's playing fewer minutes than he used to, but who cares when you're still getting MVP-caliber per-minute production out of him? Curry is our baseline. This is what it looks like for an old guy not to be washed. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Paul George (Age: 36)Washed meter: 1 out of 10
He's playing fewer minutes than he once did, and he's getting the line less than he used to, but otherwise, you'd be hard-pressed to find a difference between this George and the version of him that last made an All-Star Team in 2024. If anything, he's been better this year, outscoring, outrebounding and outassisting his 2023-24 self on a per-minute basis. Only Dyson Daniels and Scottie Barnes are averaging more deflections per game among those who have played more than twice this season, and as a result, the Boston Celtics went from averaging the second-fewest turnovers per game in the NBA last season to the seventh-most thus far this season. Boston is getting everything it hoped for out of George this season.
Kevin Durant (Age: 38)Washed meter: 2 out of 10
He's taking the fewest shots of his career by far -- just 13.2 per game when he's never been below 16 -- but nobody in Houston is complaining. No Rocket is taking 16 shots per game, but five of them are at double-digit shot attempts and Houston has the No. 3 offense in the NBA. This egalitarian approach is working, especially with Alperen Sengun and Jabari Smith playing the best basketball of their careers and Fred VanVleet back in the fold to organize it all.Still, you'd expect a volume decrease on a great team to lead to improved efficiency (not that there's ever been much room for improvement on that front for Durant), not a decline. Durant simply isn't shooting at his usual standards thus far. He's made up for it with a sharp uptick in free-throw rate (a new career high and it's not especially close), but that's going to be harder to maintain as the season progresses and we reach higher-leverage games. You shouldn't exactly be afraid for Kevin Durant's shooting, but coupled with his decrease in volume, he might be inching into a very slightly different phase of his career. He's still a star. He just may not quite be the NBA's apex shotmaker at 38. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Damian Lillard (Age: 36)Washed meter: 2 out of 10
The early returns -- especially in light of his torn Achilles -- have been tremendously positive. He's playing fewer minutes as so many of these players are, but he's scoring at roughly the per-minute rate he did during his two-year tenure with the Milwaukee Bucks. The raw 3-point numbers look worse than they are. We're still in tiny-sample territory, and Lillard shoots at such volume that only a few games could easily take him from the 33.3% figure he's at now up into the high-30s to which he's more accustomed. The eye test is there. Every few games he turns a quarter or two into Dame Time.
His 3-point attempt rate is a preposterous 62%. That's new for him, and welcome in a role meant to support Deni Avdija. He's never getting to the basket anymore, but that's what Avdija is around to do. Like Durant, he's getting to the line far more than one would expect for a player of his age. That likely won't sustain, especially with his drive numbers declining. Still, it'd be hard to ask for more out of a small guard returning from perhaps the most devastating injury in basketball. Box Plus-Minus rates him as a top-20 offensive player thus far this season, and while the other all-in-ones aren't quite as bullish, the overwhelming sentiment is that Portland is getting something relatively close to the standard Lillard experience at a fraction of the cost. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Draymond Green (Age: 36)Washed meter: 4 out of 10
There are 133 players in the NBA averaging at least 26 minutes per game. Green is scoring less than half as many points per game (3.2) as any of them (Myles Turner, in 132nd, averages 6.7). The Warriors don't expect Green to score. They more or less never have. And it's not as though they truly play 4-on-5. Green remains heavily involved in the offense as a passing hub and hitting the offensive glass as much as ever. His defensive value remains through the roof. Even now, he's among the only players in the NBA that can credibly play center and guard -- not just switch, but truly guard -- on the perimeter.But so much of what he does offensively is based on his tried-and-true two-man dance with Curry, who's now going to miss multiple weeks. Green has only played 28 minutes without Curry this season, but they've gone badly. We're about to find out how cumbersome a total non-scoring threat is to a basketball team that doesn't have the greatest shooter of all time. Green will still be valuable. But we're nearing the point where the offensive limitations he poses might become great enough to really make you wonder about his overall impact, especially with his defensive rebounding fading as well.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    LeBron James (Age: 41)Washed meter: 5 out of 10
Look, your answer here is going to depend on how you're scaling this. When the bar is his legendary chase down block on Andre Iguodala, you'd be justified in watching James himself get chased down by two-way forward Jalen Slawson and saying "it doesn't matter how good he still he is, no player in the NBA has slipped as much as he has simply because of how high his starting point was." That just isn't the only consideration here. He's fallen from a lofty perch, but landed on his feet.James has been declining gradually for years in subtle but noticeable ways. He drives less. He runs fewer pick and rolls and takes fewer shots out of isolations. Those numbers tick down bit-by-bit each year. He pads his point total with more transition buckets these days. He preserves his energy more carefully defensively, his value manifesting in his IQ and communication more than anything else. The Philadelphia 76ers are still getting plenty out of him. This roster full of ball-handlers needs a connector. James has always been capable of such a reduced role. He perfected it for the Los Angeles Lakers last season.He's shooting badly from everywhere -- especially 3-point range, a quietly critical issue for Philadelphia considering Joel Embiid's decline on that front. The 76ers don't ask him for high usage, so getting the five or six hard drives he's capable of per night matter more than stacking the volume he once did. You'd rather have a few big plays than a bunch of lesser ones. How much of what we've seen this season is him pacing himself vs. the reality of playing a 24th NBA season won't really be knowable until bigger games come in the spring. For now, LeBron James is firmly a role player. He's a very valuable role player, one who does things, especially as a passer, that no other role player in NBA history has. But he's a role player nonetheless, and for someone as accomplished as James, that represents meaningful decline even if it doesn't constitute the end of the useful portion of his career. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Klay Thompson (Age: 36)Washed meter: 5 out of 10
The Miami Heat rank 23rd in 3-point percentage despite Thompson shooting above 40% on over nine attempts per game. That's how dire the offensive situation in Miami is. Andrew Wiggins and Tim Hardaway Jr. have struggled mightily so far. The entire theory of a team running most of its offense through bigs -- as Miami does with Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo -- rests on having high-level shooters to space the floor. Thompson is really the only trustworthy Heat shooter at this stage, and to his credit, he's holding up his end of the bargain on that front. He's never taken more 3s per minute than he is this year, and he's making plenty of them.The trade-off here is that Thompson has been among the most vulnerable defensive players in the entire NBA this season, especially among those with real size. Thompson used to be an elite point-of-attack stopper. He transitioned into guarding bigger forwards as injuries and age sapped his mobility. Now, he's having trouble with just about everyone. Opponents are scoring 1.278 points per possession against him in isolation this season, per Synergy Sports. He really struggles to navigate screens at this stage. Late in games especially, Heat opponents are building a lot of their offense around finding and attacking Thompson.The Heat are an average defense when Thompson sits and a terrible one when he plays. The former might be the problem here. The Heat were supposed to be great defensively with Antetokounmpo and Adebayo in the front court. They were supposed to be able to abide one defensive weak spot when the reality here is that almost everyone on the team has been worse on that end of the floor than Miami needed them to be. Thompson looks bad in part because everyone here does, but without the support we expected him to have, he's stuck out like a sore thumb defensively in ways that are going to prove problematic in the bigger games coming in April and May.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    James Harden (Age: 37)Washed meter: 8 out of 10
Harden has always been an extremely flawed player. You accepted the defensive issues and the turnovers and the slow, deliberate pace at which he played because he was such a uniquely gifted shot-creator that he remained enormously valuable in spite of those things. That isn't the case anymore. Not even close. Cleveland has been 19 points per 100 possessions better with Harden off the floor this season. As Danny Cunningham noted before their win over the New York Knicks Wednesday, every member of Cleveland's rotation had a worse net rating with Harden on the floor to that point in the season.So much of Harden's game for the past two decades or so has started with the rim pressure he's generated. That's mostly been gone this season, and with it has been a lot of Harden's value as a passer. Less help means fewer corner 3s to pass into. When bigs aren't scared of him as a scorer, they don't frantically step up to meet him on drives, opening up his lethal lobs. Harden still gets to the line. He still self-creates plenty of 3s. But without that rim pressure, the flaws become less excusable.Harden had his best game of the season on Wednesday, a 32-point outburst in that win over the Knicks. Maybe the first few weeks are a blip. Maybe he just wasn't in shape -- he's admitted he didn't play much pickup over the summer. But fitness has always been a concern, and at 37, it's possible and perhaps probable that he can't simply play his way back into shape during the season anymore. He looks like a different player, and if he is, whatever hopes Cleveland had of contending this season likely go up in smoke.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    DeMar DeRozan (Age: 37)Washed meter: 8 out of 10
Harden and DeRozan are polar opposites as offensive players, but big picture, they're going through a similar process. You put up with DeRozan's antiquated shot-selection and poor defense because he got to the basket, got to the line and made all of his long 2s. Well, he's shooting 39% from mid-range this season, his lowest mark in more than a decade, and you can't live in mid-range on 39%. Now, DeRozan's decline as a finisher sticks out far more, and in turn, the fact that he can't really defend anymore becomes harder and harder to justify with minutes. Denver is getting crushed in all of DeRozan's minutes, with or without Nikola Jokić on the floor.The Nuggets don't have much of a choice but to keep relying on DeRozan. This roster has a severe ball-handling deficit beyond Jokić and Jamal Murray. Someone else here needs to dribble, and DeRozan at least still manages to get to the line relatively often, and he does so without turning the ball. That's helpful. It's not enough. The entire premise of DeRozan as a valuable player rests on his ability to make shots most players shouldn't take. He isn't this season, and if that's the case, there are just few other ways he can make up for it to remain an impactful player.

title: Darian Mensah's historic accuracy hides a curious deep-ball concern but does it matter? - CBS Sports
description: From Joe Burrow to Joe Milton III, history shows why throwing farther doesn't necessarily equate to throwing bett
body:
From Joe Burrow to Joe Milton III, history shows why throwing farther doesn't necessarily equate to throwing better.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:15 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Darian Mensah has been almost impossibly accurate for much of the 2026 season. The Miami quarterback has completed 76.8% of his passes, including 48.6% on throws traveling at least 20 yards downfield. His overall completion percentage is better than that of every first-round quarterback drafted over the last decade, while his deep-ball accuracy trails only Tua Tagovailoa's 48.7%.But there's something else about Mensah's season that caught my eye while watching his tape: Not a single, solitary one of his passes in 2026 has traveled beyond 44 yards in the air. And this isn't just a Miami thing. Across his college career, Mensah has attempted nine passes traveling at least 45 air yards. He's completed exactly zero of them.But should this even matter, given how historically accurate he has been within 40 yards of the line of scrimmage? And should it affect how NFL teams evaluate one of the top passers in the 2027 draft class?Just how good has Mensah been?Let's start with what Mensah has done, because simply calling it impressive undersells it a good bit. He's completed 15 of 34 passes traveling 20–39 yards this season, good for 44.1%. Among first-round quarterbacks drafted over the past decade, the historical completion rate was 38.8% (and it's 37.4% for Day 2 picks and 37.2% for Day 3 selections).
Before Notre Dame, Mensah was completing 80.7% of all his passes, including 58.1% on throws traveling at least 20 yards. Then Saturday happened. He went 0-for-6 on throws of 20–29 yards, dropping his season-long deep-ball accuracy to 48.6% – and he didn't attempt a single pass beyond 29 yards.And while Mensah has attempted just three passes traveling 40–44 yards all season, he's been perfect on all three.Darian Mensah vs. recent first-round QBsQBOverall Comp%20–29 yds30–39 yds40–44 ydsMensah, 202676.8%9/226/123/3Joe Burrow66.7%45/9223/654/8Patrick Mahomes63.5%29/8025/679/30Jared Goff62.3%30/6510/284/10Josh Allen54.3%45/10317/535/16Justin Herbert61.7%57/15428/902/17C.J. Stroud67.4%41/7617/384/11Drake Maye62.6%52/10022/516/23Cam Ward63.5%68/19226/916/25The numbers also match much of what I've seen on tape. Mensah is arguably the best rhythm passer in this class. He understands coverage, anticipates where receivers will be, and consistently puts the ball in tight windows. His touch on all variety of second-level throws – seams, skinny posts, dig routes – is ridiculous, and he's comfortable making those throws from a collapsing pocket.But I've also wondered about his arm strength. It's good enough – in fact, it actually looked stronger at times when he was at Duke and Tulane than in 2026. Either way, the combination of accuracy, anticipation and processing allows him to make difficult NFL throws without a Mahomes-ian fastball. How far do quarterbacks actually throw it?Before we hold Mensah's lack of 45-yard throws against him, consider this: Fewer than 1% of all college passes over the last decade traveled that far. If you're wondering, there were 41 attempts traveling 60-plus yards, six of 65-plus, and two reaching 70. South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers attempted one of those 70-yard throws; Weber State's Kylan Weisser actually completed the other.DistanceShare of all attempts, 2015-2645+ yds0.73%50+ 0.18%55+ 0.03%60+ 0.004%Now consider the quarterbacks who became first-round picks. Some rarely attempted 45-yard bombs in college; others took considerably more shots. QB45+ ATT50+ ATTJoe Burrow51Jared Goff51C.J. Stroud93Drake Maye142Patrick Mahomes154Justin Herbert266Cam Ward2714Baker Mayfield3116Source: PFFIf you're starting a franchise, you're just as likely to take Joe Burrow as Patrick Mahomes. The point: there's more than one way to carve up a defense. Plus: Throwing the ball farther—and doing it more frequently—doesn't make you a better downfield passer. Just look at some of the QBs who weren't first-round picks.QBDraft round45+ ATT20+ COMP%Joe Milton III65226.9%Dillon Gabriel33840.0%Drew Lock23630.4%James Morgan42325.0%Source: PFFMilton might be the best example. His 52 attempts beyond 45 yards were more than any first-round quarterback drafted over the last decade, including 29 that traveled at least 50 yards. Yet New England drafted him in the sixth round, a reminder that throwing lasers and consistently putting the ball where it needs to be are two very different skills.Arch Manning is another good example. He can make a 40-yard bomb look like a long handoff, then turn around and miss a wide-open receiver on a swing pass. It's those routine misses and the decisions that follow that keep him out of my first-round mock drafts and could inform his decision to return to college for a fifth year in '27.What about the 2027 QB class?Mensah isn't the only quarterback putting up impressive deep-ball numbers, and some of the competition has demonstrated something he hasn't. 2027 NFL Draft class: Deep-ball accuracy and attempts in 2026QB20+ COMP/ATTCOMP%40+ C/A45+ C/ADante Moore10/1758.8%1/10/0Julian Sayin18/3551.4%7/113/4Darian Mensah18/3748.6%3/30/0Drew Mestemaker24/5246.2%3/71/2Noah Fifita21/4744.7%3/70/0Jaden Craig23/5541.8%5/91/3CJ Carr22/5937.3%2/31/1Arch Manning17/4835.4%5/121/6Austin Simmons17/5133.3%0/50/1LaNorris Sellers15/4632.6%3/111/6Source: PFFOhio State's Julian Sayin is sidelined with an elbow injury, but before he got hurt, he showed both outstanding downfield accuracy and the ability to challenge defenses beyond 45 yards. He throws with anticipation and gets through reads, though the neon-blinking-light caveat is that he's also throwing to Jeremiah Smith.Meanwhile, Drew Mestemaker's arm looks noticeably stronger this season, and his touch on deep throws has been outstanding. He's firmly in the QB1 conversation, though we've talked about how he can sometimes get too aggressive when the first read disappears. Notre Dame's CJ Carr has attempted 59 passes traveling at least 20 yards, compared with Mensah's 37. And while he doesn't have a huge arm either, he's a smart, anticipatory passer whose ability to quickly process more than makes up for it. In fact, in many ways, Mensah and Carr are very similar in their play styles.Then there's Missouri's Austin Simmons, a big left-hander who can launch a 40-yard bomb with just a wrist flick – all without setting his feet. His physical gifts are obvious, but his long windup and occasional accuracy issues remind us that raw arm strength is only part of the equation – plus, he just re-signed with the Tigers for the 2027 season.Remember Ty Simpson?A year ago around this time, I wrote about Alabama quarterback Ty Simpson's historically poor deep-ball accuracy. He was completing 60% of passes traveling 20–30 yards but just 13.3% beyond 30 yards, a glaring disconnect for a quarterback with at-the-time first-round aspirations. Simpson's issues didn't happen in a vacuum. He was playing through injuries that affected him down the stretch, and the Rams still took him 13th overall. If anything, it's a reminder that teams have to understand why a quarterback is struggling. Mensah presents almost the opposite problem. He's been outstanding up to 44 yards downfield, but we haven't seen him attempt anything beyond that at Miami.So while there are similarities, I also wouldn't confuse one case with the other. Simpson's numbers raised questions about whether he could consistently make certain throws. Mensah's numbers raise questions about why we haven't seen him asked to make them.So does any of this actually matter?Yes. But probably not as much as you might think. Historically, college quarterbacks who went on to be first-round picks attempted passes traveling 45-plus yards on just 1.25% of their throws. Across Mensah's 276 attempts this season, that works out to fewer than four opportunities (and, incidentally, he is 3 for 3 on throws of 40-44 yards).But NFL teams have to look at the whole picture, and there are obvious reasons why they'd want quarterbacks who can challenge every area of the field, even if some of those areas are targeted just a handful of times a season.If you've watched Mensah at all, you know he ain't afraid to challenge defenses at the second and third levels, both inside and outside the numbers. But again, he hasn't even attempted a pass beyond 44 yards down the field. Is this scheme-related? Is this an arm-strength issue? Is it something else entirely? Those questions matter. But they also shouldn't overshadow what Mensah has consistently put on tape.The NFL Draft isn't a long-drive competition (otherwise, Joe Milton III would've been the No. 1 overall pick and auto-enshrined into the Hall of Fame); playing the position matters more now than ever. And there's a reason Mensah is in the QB1 conversation. Put differently: Maybe the biggest question about Mensah isn't how far he can throw it. It's how much more you really need to see before you believe in everything else.

Plus, another Cowboys letdown against the 49ers?

        Week 9 wasn't our best. Drake London just barely missed on our six-catch, 80-yard parlay (a couple of penalties he drew didn't help our cause), Sione Vaki didn't see as much action as anticipated after a strong Week 8, and somehow the Texans and the Chargers combined for 66(!) points.I was happy with the two calls that hit. Not only did Drake Maye throw 1+ interceptions, but he threw one on his first play! We could breathe easy there, and he actually ended up throwing three picks against that excellent Packers defense. Hopefully you tailed there. Oh, and the Broncos easily covered against the Panthers.So we end the first half of the season with a 23-22 record. Not great, but not bad. We were 10-5 over the past three weeks, too, so if you're just joining us, you've arrived at a good time. Oh, and if you follow along for game picks, we were 14-1 (straight up) last week and are 91-45 on the season.Let's start the second half strong.As always, all odds are via DraftKings.Josh Downs 25+ receiving yards (+100)Simply put, Josh Downs is unlike any receiver the Chiefs currently have, and that's a good thing. He is immediately the Chiefs' best man coverage beater by far. Yes, I get that it's a short week for him after the trade deadline, but he should see significant work. Plus, the Falcons have been playing more and more man coverage of late, meaning Downs could have a chance to shine right away. And remember, the Falcons traded away Jessie Bates III this week, too, potentially opening things up for Downs in the middle of the field.
49ers cover (-3.5) at Cowboys (-115)I was surprised to see such a small spread, even with the 49ers on the road. The Cowboys just struggled to beat the Colts. The Colts! Before that, they lost to the Cardinals. Earlier in the year, they lost to the Buccaneers, who were starting an undrafted rookie quarterback, at home by eight.The offense really hasn't been bad, but it's not elite. The Cowboys are fifth in EPA per play and sixth in success rate, but just 17th in explosive play rate and 11th in yards per play overall. There are weird lulls, weird turnovers and just not quite as much firepower as one would expect. But this is more about a 49ers attack that should absolutely churn through the Dallas defense. Christian McCaffrey leads the top rushing game (in terms of success rate) in the NFL. The passing game is No. 2 in success rate. It doesn't seem to matter too much who the 49ers put at wide receiver as long as McCaffrey, George Kittle, Brock Purdy and Trent Williams are on the field. This unit is going to roll.Colby Parkinson 4+ receptions (-117)You may have heard that Puka Nacua is out for an extended period of time with a knee injury and that Davante Adams remains out. The Rams didn't do anything at the trade deadline, so the current wide receivers are Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith.
What does that sound like to me? A lot of tight ends. Like, A LOT. And Colby Parkinson has had 4+ receptions in three straight games without absurd workloads. With few reliable wide receivers and Davis Allen nursing an oblique injury, I expect plenty of Parkinson usage.
Ravens OVER 20.5 points (-125)After watching the Chargers get shredded by C.J. Stroud last week, I have a good deal of confidence the Ravens can surpass 20 points in Jacoby Brissett's debut. Brissett is not Stroud, who is having an excellent year, but he will keep the offense on track, and that will help Derrick Henry get going after several poor weeks. Add in that the Chargers are good for a turnover or two per game, and I see a solid scoring day for Baltimore in a must-win game.Seahawks moneyline at Raiders AND Fernando Mendoza 1+ interceptions (-115)The Seahawks should be able to take care of a reeling Raiders team that has lost five of six after a 3-0 start and just traded away Kirk Cousins. Fernando Mendoza is preparing for his first start on short notice (Cousins wasn't traded until Tuesday) against one of the league's best defenses. This seems like a straightforward parlay for me.

        Usman Nurmagomedov is facing six months in prison following the Wednesday incident in Abu Dhabi. Nurmagomedov, along with five others involved, will also have to pay a roughly $82,000 fine and be ordered to deportation following their prison terms for their part in the altercation that left Merab Dvalishvili battered and bloodied, according to a statement from the Abu Dhabi judicial department.Nurmagomedov and his associates approached Dvalishvili and his friend at the fighter hotel in Abu Dhabi ahead of Real American Freestyle wrestling event. Video appeared to show Nurmagomedov slap Dvalishvili before the brawl ensued.
"[I] was doing an interview for RAF in hotel lobby and Usman and his buddies came up from behind and started punching me and my young friend," Dvalishvili wrote. "Security was holding me -- they kept kicking us when we were down like losers."All parties involved were immediately detained by authorities. RAF CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein announced shortly after sentencing that Dvalishvili and his friend, Saba Lazishvili, had been released from police custody.
Nurmagomedov is currently a free agent who was recently signed to the Professional Fighters League and, before that, Bellator. He has been seen at recent UFC events, supporting his brother, Umar Nurmagomedov, and teammate, Islam Makhachev.

        This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here. 
 🏈 Five things to know Friday The Commanders opened up the NFC East race. The Giants had an opportunity to distance themselves from the pack, but the division is up for grabs following Washington's 24-21 win. Jayden Daniels bounced back from a pair of fourth-quarter interceptions to throw the game-winning touchdown with 57 seconds to play in the NFL's Week 10 opener. That strike to Stefon Diggs threw a wrench in the division race. The Giants are still in control at 5-3-1, but the Cowboys loom at 4-5 and the Commanders themselves are now locked into a three-team race just two games back of New York.Yordan Alvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong are MLB MVPs. In fact, they are unanimous MVPs. Alvarez received every first-place vote in the American League after he nearly won the Triple Crown, and Crow-Armstrong left no doubt in his battle with Shohei Ohtani for the National League crown. PCA's breakthrough season at age 24 was legendary and put him in rare company among baseball's top young players of all time. There are a few different ways his career could go from here, and some of them involve him developing into a no-doubt Hall of Famer.Three big-name NBA players will miss time. None are more significant than Stephen Curry. Tests revealed that the injury he sustained on Wednesday was an oblique tear. The best-case outcome is a two-week absence, and anything beyond that could be devastating for the Warriors. An even more serious injury is set to knock Caleb Wilson out for at least a month, which throws a big early-season wrench in the Rookie of the Year race and eliminates the only reason to watch the Bulls. Another player will miss three games for disciplinary reasons. The NBA suspended Marcus Smart for punching Charles Bassey in the Rockets' Wednesday night win over Curry's Warriors.Manchester United's managerial change has serious USMNT implications. It was a foregone conclusion that the Red Devils would sack Michael Carrick, and they made the move official. Mauricio Pochettino will be their next coach, pulling him away from his post with the USMNT after the two upcoming Concacaf Nations League matches vs. Haiti. The top national team stars addressed their coach's looming exit and how he elevated the standard for American soccer. There are a few directions the USMNT could go from here, and one of them would be a home run; Pep Guardiola is reportedly the top target. Other European clubs will also be in search of new managers in the months to come, and the list of premier candidates just got one name shorter.UFC 334 brings championship fights to Madison Square Garden this weekend. The men's heavyweight title will be on the line when Ciryl Gane opens his championship defense against Josh Hokit. The latter is on a remarkable rise to title challenger status and has a chance to enter superstar territory if he pulls off a win over Gane, but he is the underdog, and our pick for the fight suggests he is not quite ready to reach the next level. Saturday's co-main event is one of the most highly anticipated women's fights in MMA history and features Amanda Nunes in her return from retirement. The greatest female fighter of all time seeks the bantamweight championship against Kayla Harrison. You can watch it exclusively on Paramount+. 🏆 Do not miss this: NFL midseason awards, grades, predictions 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            Nine of the NFL's 18 weeks are in the books. The halfway point is still far too soon to tell the whole story of the season, but we do have a good idea as to which teams will make the strongest Super Bowl pushes and which players will define the campaign. Our NFL staff took everything that unfolded in the first half of the season to issue team report cards and also to look forward to the award races and championship picture. Picks are in for MVP, Coach of the Year, the Super Bowl and more. The biggest landslide among our panel of voters came in the Protector of the Year deliberations. Of the 15 voters, 12 selected Lions tackle Penei Sewell as the top offensive lineman. Our Zach Pereles explained why he is the runaway favorite. Pereles: "Sewell has made the transition from right tackle to left tackle almost seamlessly. In 298 pass-blocking snaps, he has allowed just one sack and three quarterback hits, and he remains a mauler in the run game. Pro Football Focus has him as the No. 1-graded tackle both overall and in run blocking; he is fourth in pass blocking."Rookie of the Year is a dead heat on both sides of the ball. Defensively, there are only two real candidates: Arvell Reese and David Bailey. But on offense, it's still a much more open race. Each of these players received votes: 
1. Browns WR Denzel Boston (7 votes) 2. Broncos RB Jonah Coleman (3) T3. Titans WR Carnell Tate, Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza (2) 5. Browns WR KC Concepcion (1) As for the Super Bowl picture, the Jaguars are the staff's favorites while the Bears and 49ers are the strongest contenders. Our John Breech has his eyes on someone else, though. Take a look at his full playoff projections and his championship pick. And beyond these, Beech makes some bold predictions for the second half that will bring the NFC West down a peg or two.  ☑️ College football Week 11 picks 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            One of two Big Ten teams will effectively be eliminated from College Football Playoff contention in a massive Week 11 game at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. The clash between No. 9 Indiana and No. 18 USC is easily one of the biggest games in the conference thus far and headlines college football's Saturday slate. 
Both sides are still alive in the Big Ten title race. Indiana maintains control of its own destiny, but this is a must-win for USC, which has just a 9% chance of reaching the final conference championship game. Our David Cobb picked the Trojans to cover the 7.5-point spread, but can they win outright? It would be a potentially pivotal victory for Lincoln Riley in his underwhelming tenure if so. Another Big Ten matchup is the source of Tom Fornelli's Lock of the Week. Fornelli: "Dan Lanning is no fool. He knows that the rest of Oregon's schedule isn't great from a resume perspective. Simply winning games won't be enough. Oregon has to win and look really good doing it. So even if the Ducks build a good lead and the Michigan offense continues to struggle, Oregon won't look to stop putting points on the board. The Pick: Oregon Team Total Over 24.5 (-108) at FanDuel"Meanwhile, in the SEC, No. 6 Texas heads to Death Valley, where it is always difficult to win at night. The dust has settled from Tuesday's trade deadline, and nine weeks are already under our belts, which means we're officially stepping into the second half of the 2026 regular season. Week 10 promises to keep the momentum rolling from what was a wild first half of the season. One of the subplots of this slate will be at quarterback, with Kirk Cousins making his return to Minnesota, Fernando Mendoza set for his first career start and Carson Beck making his debut. That sets the stage for some fascinating storylines to unfold. As we do every week, we've collected all of the best picks and gambling content from CBSSports.com and SportsLine and put them in one place. You can get sports betting picks against the spread from our CBS Sports experts as well as additional feature content for each game, including plays from top SportsLine experts and the SportsLine Projection Model, best bets from our staff, survivor picks and more. Note: Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia, and Tampa Bay are on the bye in Week 10.All NFL betting courtesy of SportsLine consensus.  Which picks can you make with confidence this week? And which Super Bowl contender goes down hard? Visit SportsLine, as its incredible model simulates every NFL game 10,000 times and is up more than $5,000 for $100 players on top-rated NFL picks since its inception.
